questions.prompt: What does 3/4 of a pizza mean?
options: 3 slices out of a possible 4 whole pizzas
questions.explanation: The denominator 4 names the equal parts the whole is split into; the numerator 3 counts the parts taken.
questions.misconception: Reading the fraction backwards (4 of 3) or thinking the parts are whole pizzas mixes up which number counts the equal parts of the ONE whole.

questions.prompt: Why must the parts of a fraction be equal?
options: So each part names the same size piece of the whole
Because the numerator needs matching slices
They do not have to be equal
questions.explanation: Equal parts make the fraction an honest measure — 1/4 means exactly the same size piece no matter which part you take.
questions.misconception: Neatness is not the reason — if the pieces are uneven, '3 of 4' no longer names a fixed amount of the whole.

questions.prompt: There are 8 marbles and you have 3 of them. What fraction of the marbles do you have?
questions.explanation: The group is 8 marbles (denominator) and you have 3 (numerator), so the fraction is 3/8.
questions.misconception: 8/3 is the inverted (wrong) order, and 5/8 counts the marbles you do NOT have — a fraction of a group uses the total as the denominator.

questions.explanation: 2/3 is less than 1 because the numerator is smaller than the denominator — you have fewer parts than the whole.
questions.misconception: 4/4 equals exactly 1, and fractions with a numerator larger than the denominator (7/3, 5/2) are greater than 1.

questions.prompt: Which fraction is written as 'three fifths'?
questions.misconception: 5/3 says 'five thirds', not 'three fifths' — the word order matches numerator first, then denominator.
